literal_evidence.quote: it is challenging to get a 2-3 day period with good drying weather and no rainfall. June is the rainiest month of the year (averaging about 4 inches), resulting in soils that are wetter than later in the summer. Moist soils increase drying times of cut forage. The chance of receiving at least a small amount of rainfall (>0.04”) on any given day is about 40% (i.e., 60% chance of no rain), so there is a narrow window for drying; the probability of 2 and 3 days of dry weather in a row in June is 36 and 22%, respectively. Rainfall at any time after cutting of hay can result in significant losses of dry matter and nutrients. These losses are greatest for partially dried forage due to leaf shattering, leaching, and prolonged respiration. Total dry matter losses are possible, but often range from 20 to 30%.
